brand.purpose: The serif wordmark in the top bar.

narrative.purpose: The preview text — the finished chart, 14.5px, max 75ch, 1.75 leading.

line-label.purpose: The name at the head of a worksheet row, right-aligned in the 8.75rem label column.

field-label.purpose: The inline key before a value, 11.5px Placeholder Grey, right-aligned in the fixed 8.75rem label column.

value.purpose: Filled field text at 13.5px; ink at weight 500 once accepted.

control.purpose: Text inside buttons, selects and text inputs, 13px.

badge.purpose: The 11px, weight 500 open-item count beside Copy.

keyhint.purpose: Mono hints: the 11px hint strip and status bar, Pencil Grey.

keyhint-inline.purpose: The 10.5px mono hint inside a focused row, aligned to the value column.

counter.purpose: Mono tabular character count against the 4,000 cap, 12.5px, at the foot of the preview.

shadows.name: focused-row
shadows.purpose: The row with keyboard focus; the only in-flow shadow.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: A line or section being dragged or keyboard-grabbed.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: The modal card over a warm scrim, rgba(35,32,26,.38).

shadows.name: cursor-ring
shadows.purpose: The pill under the keyboard cursor.

motion.name: hover-reveal
motion.purpose: Drag handle and delete × fade in on row hover; always visible on touch. The paragraph badge uses the same fade (hidden at rest unless moved).

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: panes stack, preview pane static, top-bar controls full width.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: At or above: pane gap and padding grow to 20px.

narrative.overview:
A pocket notebook the medic writes in after the call. The page is cream, the ink is one near-black pencil, and the proposals the builder makes are written faintly in italic until the medic overwrites or accepts them. Nothing on the page competes for attention because nothing on the page is decoration: every mark is either a label, a value, a rule, or a key hint. The narrative preview is the notebook's fair-copy page, set in serif at a reading leading, while the worksheet beside it is the working page in a small sans.

The mood is calm and clerical. Calm: one accent, used only for the two things that interrupt the writing (starting a new call, and the open items that gate Copy — a red chip wherever a field is still missing). Clerical: small uppercase section heads, labels right-aligned in one ledger column with their values beside them, hairline rules between sections, a monospace strip of key hints. Density is deliberate — a 13.5px body and 13.5px values on a laptop put a whole shell section on one screen, and the tool is driven from the keyboard, so rows are tight and controls are short.

Selection is never a new hue. A chosen pill inverts to solid ink on cream; a focused row gains an ink border; a confirmed value turns from faint grey to full ink at weight 500. Clinical meaning, when it exists, borrows the three tones the chart itself uses — given (green), withheld (amber), fired (red) — and only on settled decisions.
keyCharacteristics: One ink: near-black is both the text color and the selection fill; there is no brand blue.
Proposals are faint italic; acceptance turns them upright, full ink, weight 500.
Hairline warm-grey rules structure the page; shadows appear only on things that float.
Serif for what the medic reads (wordmark, narrative); sans for what the medic fills; mono for hints and counts.
Light mode only, embedded fonts, no motion beyond a 120 ms hover reveal.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Selection, focus, and primary action are all expressed by Pencil Ink — a fill, a border, or a full-strength text color. No hue is introduced to mean "chosen".

rules.name: The Settled Tone Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red appear only on a decision the medic has made (given / withheld / fired) or on a gate the medic must clear (open items, the cap). A proposal is never colored; it is faint and italic.

rules.name: The Red Interrupt Rule
rules.body: Outside the clinical tones, red is reserved for New call and the open items that gate Copy. An open item is one red chip wherever it appears: a missing field on the worksheet wears the same red-wash chip as its blank in the preview — red text, red wash, a 1.5px red underline, weight 500 (the worksheet's `.ws-amber` state class keeps its old name). Nothing else on the page is red.

rules.name: The Two-Weight Rule
rules.body: The sans has 400 and 500 and nothing heavier. Emphasis beyond 500 is done with ink (color), case, or spacing — never with bold.

rules.name: The Italic Means Proposal Rule
rules.body: Italic in the worksheet or preview always means "the builder's suggestion, not yet accepted" (proposed values, dashed proposal pills, proposal placeholders, unattested defaults) — or, for the empty preview's one placeholder line, "nothing is written yet". Do not use italic for emphasis or for titles.

rules.name: The Paper-Over-Paper Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the document flow casts a shadow except the focused row. A shadow means the element is floating above the page, and it is always warm brown.

dos: Do show selection by inverting to Pencil Ink (#23201A) on Cream Page (#F7F4ED); the on-pill, the Copy button, and the Polish toggle all use this one move.
Do write every proposal in Pencil Grey (#5F594C) italic with a dashed border or underline, and turn it upright and full ink (weight 500) the moment it is accepted.
Do keep text inputs as underlines (1.5px #948870), not boxes; boxes are for selects, buttons, and pills.
Do keep every control border and input rule at Rule Strong (#948870) or darker, so it holds 3:1 against the page.
Do reach for the warm-brown shadow (rgba(60,50,30,…)) only when something floats — popup, lifted drag, modal.
Do keep the sans at 400 and 500 and the serif at 400–600; set the narrative in Source Serif 4 at 1.75 leading.
Do reveal secondary controls (drag handle, delete ×) on hover with the 120 ms opacity fade, and leave them visible on touch.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue; blue, teal, or purple do not exist in this system.
Don't color a value that the medic has not settled — green, amber, and red belong to given, withheld, and fired decisions and to the open-item and cap gates only.
Don't use red anywhere except New call, delete-on-hover, the open-item gate (including the worksheet's missing-field chip), and the fired tone.
Don't use italic for emphasis or titles; italic means "proposed".
Don't add dark mode, motion beyond the 120 ms hover reveal, or shadows in the document flow.
Don't replace the hairline Rule Faint (#DFD8C9) structure with cards; sections are rules and indents, not boxes.
